brief.headline: Lock in a second source from the five strong alternates and ask Rachana to match the typical market price of ₹0.85–0.95/pc for caps — we're currently at market-fair, but volume gives us room to push toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc.

priceAsk.summary: Ask Rachana to quote ₹0.65–0.80/pc on 28 mm caps at higher volume, down from the current market-fair band of ₹0.85–0.95/pc.
priceAsk.basis: The open-market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The verdict says there is modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — so we can justify pushing down if we commit more volume or simplify the design.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 days after receipt — it already frees up ₹3.65 L of cash for us each year compared to paying on delivery.

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana Plastics publishes no financials, so we cannot see how healthy or cash-tight they are. Our ₹44.37 L annual spend is meaningful to a private converter, but we don't know what share of their revenue that is. Without their numbers, we lean on the fact that we have five credible alternate suppliers — two listed (Mold-Tek, Manjushree) and three private — plus six manufacturer and recycler leads to qualify. That gives us the confidence to ask for the lower end of the market band and to insist on a second source.

evidence.point: We spend ₹44.37 L a year with Rachana on rigid plastic packaging.
The open-market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap runs ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc.
The market verdict says our price is market-fair, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec.
Paying 30 days after receipt instead of on delivery frees up ₹3.65 L of cash for us each year.
HDPE resin import unit value stands at 87.61 ₹/kg — a public benchmark for the raw material they buy.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms; the top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B (73/100) — makes pails, containers and pharma packaging; strong and profitable.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging at ₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C (51/100) — broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Rachana publishes no financials, so we are flying blind on their cash position and stability — watch for signs of delivery trouble and move fast to qualify a second source.
Pushing too hard on price without locking in an alternate first could leave us exposed if Rachana walks or stumbles — line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek before the next round.
The market-ask verdict gives us 'modest headroom' only at higher volume or looser spec — if we cannot commit more volume or relax the design, the ₹0.65–0.80/pc target may not stick.
The six marketBackups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify — verify each before sending an RFQ; do not treat them as approved sources yet.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a second source for caps and bottles this quarter, and we want to make sure your pricing reflects the volume we're giving you — the market shows room to move toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc at scale.
